summary: Sends CHOP audio channels to an output device with driver, output layout, volume, pan, clamp, and buffer controls.
key_concepts: Audio Device Out CHOP sends CHOP audio channels to a selected playback device.
Driver and Device choose the output backend and playback device, including system audio or ASIO where supported.
Buffer Length adds output delay but helps keep the audio queue full and reduce crackling or popping.
Multiple input channels are routed to enabled speaker outputs in input-channel order.
Reliable audio output depends on frame time staying below the audio buffer and CHOP maximum time-slice limits.

key_params.name: errormissing
key_params.note: Raise an error if the selected output device is missing

key_params.name: adjustspeed
key_params.note: Adjust playback speed to maintain output sync

key_params.name: clampoutput
key_params.note: Clamp output samples to valid range

key_params.name: cookalways
key_params.note: Cook every frame even if not otherwise requested

common_gotchas: Audio output is device-specific and can fail silently if the selected device disappears unless errormissing is enabled.
Low buffer lengths reduce latency but increase dropout risk.
Clamp Output can hide upstream clipping problems; use meters or Audio Dynamics when level matters.
Channel routing must match the device speaker/output layout, especially for surround or multichannel systems.
